designs.name: Codex Workbench
designs.bestFor: Tablet power-editing and tuning loadouts without losing roster context.
designs.direction: Library → persistent roster tree, live detail pane and a validation rail; optional smart search overlays it.
designs.interaction: Select in the tree, edit on the right, watch legality update in the rail. Flip on smart search for type-to-add and AI suggestions.
designs.tradeoff: Shines on tablet; on phone it falls back to a more conventional drill-in.

groups.label: Product UI
groups.description: Portable product foundations and components intended for the React Native application.

reactNative.behavior: Expose semantic tokens rather than CSS variable names.
reactNative.accessibility: Every text/background pair must meet WCAG AA contrast.

reactNative.behavior: Map roles to platform fonts and scalable type sizes.
reactNative.accessibility: Support font scaling without truncating critical values.

reactNative.behavior: Use the native status bar and safe-area insets; do not recreate this preview.
reactNative.accessibility: Keep content outside unsafe display regions.

reactNative.behavior: Respect safe areas and keep roster progress visible while editing. Plan 3C-2: the main budget stays fixed above the tree; other limited costs expand when the budget block is tapped; limits of 0 with nothing used are left out.
reactNative.accessibility: Expose titles, point totals, and progress as separate readable values.

reactNative.behavior: Present as a full screen or sheet based on navigation context.
reactNative.accessibility: Focus the heading first and provide a clear dismiss action.

reactNative.behavior: Adapt pane visibility to available width; preserve the selected unit.
reactNative.accessibility: Announce pane changes and preserve logical focus order.

reactNative.behavior: Progressively reveal game system, points, searchable faction and force pickers, then roster name.
reactNative.accessibility: Associate labels, hints, errors, and selected state with each control; trap focus in picker dialogs.

reactNative.behavior: Use virtualized rows for large rosters and preserve expansion state. The current mobile read-only preview visits each force, its direct unit rows and then child forces recursively; indent child force sections by 12 pt per level so nested units remain visible and agree with the total. When missing data is installed, reopen the mounted roster and clear the previous error; a worker restart also resets the loading/error state (MR-004/005). Plan 3C-2 (built in the app): one card per slot with compact unit rows (3 pt status rail, name, muted ×count only above 1 = the unit's model count, points or the warning/error glyph instead); non-zero non-point costs in accent text beside the name; configuration sections look like any other section and their picks show what was chosen under the name (New Recruit style), no ×count and no 0 pts; unbuilt controls (Add unit/force, ⋯) are muted in place; one Add force per place the data offers it. Plan 3D: occupied, required and broken slots stay discoverable; empty max=0 slots stay hidden even with Show all. Toggle counts include only revealable optional slots, independently per force. Preserve configuration, nested force order and expansion choices across model updates; keep one virtualized tree list.
reactNative.accessibility: Expose hierarchy level, expanded state, and validation status. Announce each force toggle’s expanded state.

reactNative.behavior: Synthetic 58-slot example: 4 occupied/required/broken sections, 11 optional sections behind a per-force toggle and 43 empty unavailable sections omitted in both modes. Add links stay suppressed in read-only rosters.
reactNative.accessibility: Announce toggle expanded state; retain hierarchy and status labels on required and broken sections.

reactNative.behavior: Use a bottom sheet on phone and anchored panel on tablet.
reactNative.accessibility: Trap focus in selectors and announce force creation results.

reactNative.behavior: Scroll detail content independently on tablet.
reactNative.accessibility: Use headings to separate configuration regions.

reactNative.behavior: Keep selection and point changes atomic.
reactNative.accessibility: Announce selection, disabled reason, and point impact.

reactNative.behavior: Present choices in a keyboard-safe bottom sheet on phone.
reactNative.accessibility: Announce group count, current choice, and price impact.

reactNative.behavior: Allow horizontal scrolling while retaining row identity.
reactNative.accessibility: Provide a linearized label for every stat value.

reactNative.behavior: Use a sheet stack with explicit back and close behavior.
reactNative.accessibility: Move focus to each opened reference and restore it on close.

reactNative.behavior: Pin above the safe area and retain the selected tab.
reactNative.accessibility: Expose tab role, selected state, and menu purpose.

reactNative.behavior: Use a native menu where available and a sheet fallback.
reactNative.accessibility: Return focus to the invoking row when dismissed.

reactNative.behavior: Built (battle-augur plan 4A): swipe right reveals Duplicate (ok tone), swipe left reveals Delete (error tone), as New Recruit. A full swipe (55% of the row, at least 1.5 action widths) or a tap on the revealed action runs it, with a light haptic at the full-swipe point. One row open at a time; scrolling or tapping elsewhere closes it. Delete asks nothing: a toast 'Deleted {name}' with Undo brings it back (only while no other edit ran since). Duplicate is quiet (UX-009). Read-only rosters have no swipe.
reactNative.accessibility: Rows expose Delete and Duplicate as accessibility actions; the unit detail header ⋯ menu offers Duplicate and Delete; the force ⋯ menu offers Delete force.

reactNative.behavior: Built (battle-augur plan 4D, DEC-004): Undo and Redo sit in the roster header before search and export, disabled when the session cannot undo/redo, hidden when read-only. Edits are sent in order; the history follows edits made on the unit detail and add sheets too. A muted caption under the budget says Saved after an edit in this visit (Saving only after 500 ms; Not saved in the error tone); its width is reserved so the budget block never moves. No save button; leaving never prompts.
reactNative.accessibility: Undo/Redo are labelled buttons with disabled state; only a failed save is announced.

reactNative.behavior: Avoid the keyboard and preserve the draft on transient errors.
reactNative.accessibility: Focus the text input and announce validation errors.

reactNative.behavior: List compatible destinations and confirm the completed move.
reactNative.accessibility: Explain why unavailable destinations are disabled.

reactNative.behavior: Built (plan 6A, Validation screen pushed over the roster; the tablet rail is later): errors, then warnings, then notes, each by roster / force; rules the app does not evaluate yet are one separate section at the end. Navigate each issue to its affected entry: a unit opens its options at the issue's selection (breadcrumbs show the path, its issues outlined); a slot, force or the roster is opened, scrolled to and highlighted for 3 s. The roster header's check line opens the list. While the rules are still being checked the list says so; after a failure the list is hidden, not left tappable.
reactNative.accessibility: Do not rely on color alone: each severity has an icon shape and its word (Error, Warning, Note) with counts; each issue is a button whose label is severity, entry and message, and whose hint says where it goes; the jumped-to row is announced and marked selected.

reactNative.behavior: Virtualize results and keep filters visible. Mobile (UX-009): an add in flight shows a spinner next to the sheet title in room kept for it; rows are not dimmed and keep their place, so repeated adds change only counts and budget.
reactNative.accessibility: Include availability and point cost in each row label.

reactNative.behavior: Optimistically add reusable configurations.
reactNative.accessibility: Differentiate favorite name from base unit name.

reactNative.behavior: Persist preference and expose entitlement state.
reactNative.accessibility: Describe the effect of enabling assistance.

reactNative.behavior: Select five neutral built-in schemes or a local imported scheme; select English or an imported language without restarting or losing navigation. Both dark and light maps pass WCAG AA.
reactNative.accessibility: Named upload buttons, checked selection rows and labelled swatches; text expands and English is always available.

reactNative.behavior: System JSON picker; worker validation and local SQLite persistence. Schemes up to 16 KiB, language packs up to 128 KiB, eight each. Replacement uses scheme ID or locale. Failed and cancelled imports preserve selection. Notices are dismissible; missing translations keep English fallback.
reactNative.accessibility: Disabled upload actions while importing; announced progress and result, icon plus text feedback, selection remains available.

reactNative.behavior: One row per installed source (version, upstream date, size) with one status chip by priority: Unreadable, Updating n%, Update available, Needs review, Ready. An updates notice offers Update all; Select enters a selection mode (update-available rows selectable, a bottom bar with Update n and Select all updates). Failed or interrupted installs keep a row with Try again / Dismiss; an interrupted update says the previous version stays in use (Try again resumes the same version, Dismiss removes the half-written data). While an update runs its new data stays hidden; the source shows once. Checks on open (hourly) and pull to refresh; the footer says when it last checked.
reactNative.accessibility: Status chips carry icon and word; selection rows are checkboxes; the selection count is announced.

reactNative.behavior: Add game data is the hub: the default collection (first sources with Install, Show all), its default listings (an organisation library and another builder's repositories, with a Default chip, DEC-024), user collections and libraries, Add a collection or library, the repository link field (DS-2), and Search GitHub (GitHub-wide search). Install starts the background install job at once (DEC-022/023).
reactNative.accessibility: Section headings; each Install button names its source; link errors are tied to the field.

reactNative.behavior: Native form sheet opened when an install or update starts: overall progress, steps (download, read, choose factions, import per faction, write) with per-step progress, Cancel (no confirmation: finished factions stay installed) and Hide. Several jobs run at once (DEC-024): the sheet shows 'n jobs', the opening job expanded and the others collapsed with their own Cancel; jobs over the measured limit show 'Waiting for another install'. Running jobs are listed first; an ended job sits after them worded as ended (Installed / Updated / Could not install / Cancelled install of {name}) with its result line, no progress and no Cancel; a new job for a source replaces that source's ended job, so a source is never listed twice (UX-011). Cancel shows 'Cancelling…' at once (UX-010). A one-time mobile-data notice makes Download on Wi-Fi only known; with it on, Download waits for Wi-Fi with Download now. 'Notify me when it finishes' asks the notification permission in context. After an update: Check rosters / Later. Hide, swipe down and Android back keep the jobs running in the worker (DEC-018, DEC-023).
reactNative.accessibility: Never show step state by colour alone (icon per state); announce step changes and the outcome, not every percent; Hide is labelled as continuing the work.

reactNative.behavior: Floating pill on every screen while a job runs: 12 pt above the tab bar, or above the bottom safe area on pushed screens and the roster workbench; screens add a bottom inset. Shows a progress ring, the job and its percent, 'n jobs' with the overall percent when several run, an accent 'needs you' state and 'Waiting for Wi-Fi'. Tap reopens the job sheet. Hidden while a sheet or the keyboard is open.
reactNative.accessibility: One button: job, percent, and 'Opens the progress'; announce only step changes and the end.

reactNative.behavior: End of a hidden job: success with View, an update with Check rosters (Report once checked and a roster changed), failure with Details (reopens the sheet in its failed state); the first mobile-data download with Wi-Fi only. Uses the built toast with an action (6 s); stacks above the job pill.
reactNative.accessibility: Announced without taking focus; the action is a named button.

reactNative.behavior: Top of the source detail: the new version and date, what changed (changed / new / removed factions, game system file) from a tree diff (nothing downloaded), a warning when rosters use a removed faction (they open read-only after the update), Update and View on GitHub. Turns into a progress row while updating, a Last update card after (Check rosters before the roster check, View report after), or a failure notice with Try again. "Using an older version · Switch to {commit}" is a row above it (Source Versions).
reactNative.accessibility: Heading for the card; the changes are a list; the progress row is one button that opens the job sheet.

reactNative.behavior: After an update (DS-5) and its offered roster check (DEC-024; built at summary level, battle-augur plan 2F part 2): summary chips, changed rosters with their changes (entries no longer in the data, totals before → after, new errors) and Open roster, rosters whose faction was removed, unchanged rosters, and the data changes by revision. Before the check: the data changes and Check rosters. Kept until the next update of the source.
reactNative.accessibility: Each roster card has a heading; changes are not colour-coded only (a label per line).

reactNative.behavior: One collection (a JSON list of repositories) or library (a GitHub organisation): description, search above eight entries, rows with Supported / Installed / Update available / Archived chips and a trailing Install, Installed, Update, Waiting or percent action. A cached copy shows offline. The menu offers Refresh, Copy link, and Remove (not for the default collection).
reactNative.accessibility: Row actions name the source; chips carry words; the offline notice is announced.

reactNative.behavior: Native form sheet: a link to a collection file or a GitHub organisation or user, Find, a preview of what was found, Add collection. A repository link offers Install it instead. Notes that collections only list repositories.
reactNative.accessibility: Label and helper tied to the field; errors announced; the preview card has a heading.

reactNative.behavior: Settings → Game data. A user preference, off by default (DEC-022: install everything). On, installs stop at Choose factions in the job sheet. Applies to the next install.
reactNative.accessibility: A switch with its label and the explanation as the hint.

reactNative.behavior: Inside the job sheet at Choose factions (Advanced installation on): Select all with a tri-state checkbox and a selected count (Deselect all when all are selected; with a search it selects the matches), search above eight factions, the built faction rows (installed ones marked and disabled), Install n factions and Cancel install. Nothing preselected. While hidden, the pill shows 'Choose factions for {name}'.
reactNative.accessibility: Select all is a checkbox with a mixed state; rows are checkboxes with documents and size in the label.

reactNative.behavior: Built in battle-augur plan 2G part 2 (DEC-024). Source detail → Versions, shown while the source has kept versions: the version in use first (ok icon, "Version {commit} · {date} · In use"), then each kept version, newest first, with its line "Version {commit} · {date} · {size}" (dates relative, as the rest of the detail) and two small buttons, Switch to this version (no confirmation; the source switches in one step, the Last update card offers Check rosters, and a toast says "Switched to version {commit}") and Delete (native alert "Delete version {commit}? Frees {size}. This cannot be undone."). When the version in use is older than a kept one, a row "Using an older version · Switch to {commit}" sits at the top of the detail, and no update is offered when the newest upstream commit is a kept version. Remove also removes the kept versions; its alert says how many rosters will open read-only and the size it frees.
reactNative.accessibility: Each version line names its commit, date and size or In use in words; Switch and Delete are named buttons (Delete destructive); a failed switch or delete shows an error notice under the group.

reactNative.behavior: UX-013 (DEC-027): the app's own centred dialog replaces every system alert and action sheet: title, optional message, actions, dimmed backdrop (theme scrim), card in the theme surface. Confirm: Cancel (secondary) first, then the action; a destructive action is filled in the error colour. Menu: the same dialog with the actions stacked and Cancel last. Backdrop tap and Android back cancel (a dialog marked must-answer ignores them). Long text wraps and the card scrolls. One host at the app root; calls return a promise.
reactNative.accessibility: Alert-dialog role announced with its title; focus moves to the dialog and returns to the invoking control; every action is a named button of at least 44 pt; keeps the safe areas and works with large text.

reactNative.behavior: UX-014 (DEC-027): severity counts stay visible; the groups of messages (unresolved references, duplicate IDs …) start folded behind Show {n} and unfold on request.
reactNative.accessibility: The Show / Hide control exposes its expanded state.

reactNative.behavior: Settings → Game data (DEC-024): Download on Wi-Fi only (off by default; made known by a one-time notice on the first mobile-data download), Job notifications (shown after the permission was asked; opens system settings when off). Keep previous versions is its own element (Keep Previous Versions Setting).
reactNative.accessibility: Switches and selectors with their explanation as the hint.

reactNative.behavior: Built in battle-augur plan 2G part 2: Settings → Game data → Keep previous versions, a padded block like Theme (history icon and heading, the line "Keep older versions of each source so you can switch back. Uses about {size} now." with the sum of the kept stores, and a segmented control Off / 1 / 2 / 3 per source). Off by default; an update keeps the store it replaces up to the setting and prunes the oldest; with Off the next update removes the kept versions.
reactNative.accessibility: The heading is a header; the segmented control is labelled Keep previous versions and each option is a radio with its value.

reactNative.component: native (iOS BGContinuedProcessingTask, Android foreground service, local notifications)
reactNative.behavior: Built in plan 2E part 3 (local module background-work): one OS session for all jobs while any runs. iOS 26+: continued-processing task (system progress with title, current step, percent; short background task when refused). Android: dataSync foreground service, silent ongoing notification "Installing {name}" / "{count} jobs" with the step or waiting state, a progress bar and Cancel; tap opens the job sheet. iOS reports its system Cancel as an expiry, so there it pauses the jobs until the app is back. A local notification says when a job ends (tap opens the sheet).
reactNative.accessibility: System surfaces; titles carry the job and percent in words.

reactNative.behavior: Built in battle-augur plan 2G parts 1–2 (DEC-024). Source removed / Faction removed: the stored roster (worker storedRoster, no data and no session): the chip row, the banner ("Read only · the data for this roster was removed" with Export and Add the data again; "Read only · {faction} is no longer in the data" with Export), the saved totals and checks "as last saved {relative date}", and the stored outline. Changed by update: the live editor on the new data, read-only (the editor header with the chip row, no add rows, unit detail read-only) and the banner with Show changes ({count}) (summary lines: Removed: {entry}, {cost}: {old} → {new}, new errors), Edit with the new data (primary) and Export as it was. When a kept version holds the roster's data, Open with version {commit} is the last choice (Faction removed, Changed by update); it opens the roster editable on that store, with the tag kept and an info notice "Opened with version {commit}" with Use the newest data instead of the banner. Buttons are small and wrap; the primary choice first.
reactNative.accessibility: The banner is announced when the roster opens; its title and body are one header; Show changes exposes its expanded state; the navigation bar label says "{name}, read only".

reactNative.behavior: Built in battle-augur plan 2G part 1: the Read only chip (lock) and the roster's data tag (Changed by update / Faction removed / Source removed) in one wrapping row under the navigation bar: at the top of a stored roster, and inside the live editor header of a changed roster. On a roster opened with a kept version only the tag shows. The navigation bar keeps the name and faction · system, without a chip (it crowded the title into the back button).
reactNative.accessibility: Chips carry words and icons; the read-only state is also in the navigation bar's label.

reactNative.behavior: Built in battle-augur plan 2G part 1: a roster without its data is shown from the stored roster and its saved snapshot, in a virtualised list. A group with "Total · as last saved {relative date}" (main total with its limit, other totals as a subtitle) and "Checks · as last saved" (No errors / {n} errors); force rows with an accent left edge (catalogue as the title, the force name below); selection rows with the name, a muted ×{count} above one, the options on one line, and the saved cost on the right when the snapshot has costs. A footer says "Costs as last saved" or "No saved costs for this roster", and that profiles and rules need the game data.
reactNative.accessibility: Each row is one element whose label has the name, quantity, options, cost and level.

reactNative.behavior: Built in battle-augur plan 2G part 1: Lists rows show the name, factions · system, "Opened {when}" / "Changed {when}" (relative), the points and the tag: Changed by update (info, circle-arrow-up) or Faction removed / Source removed (neutral, archive); Source removed replaces the earlier Data not installed chip. A Needs attention ({count}) pill above Recent shows only tagged rosters when there are any. The same tag sits in the roster's chip row. Tags clear when the roster is edited with the new data or its version is switched back.
reactNative.accessibility: Icon plus word on every tag (VA-2).

reactNative.behavior: Debounce queries, cancel stale requests, and preserve scope filters.
reactNative.accessibility: Announce result counts and async failures without stealing focus.

reactNative.behavior: Support local results while offline and report import progress.
reactNative.accessibility: Group results by type and announce import status.

reactNative.behavior: Use nested navigation with restorable tool state.
reactNative.accessibility: Provide text alternatives for charts and dice results.

reactNative.behavior: Lists header action: pick a New Recruit JSON file, import it in the engine worker, then open the roster; report unmatched parts without blocking, and send missing data to Sources. .ros/.rosz import comes later.
reactNative.accessibility: Name the action, mark it busy while importing, and announce the result notice.

reactNative.behavior: Sheet from the roster header: pick New Recruit JSON or text, preview the export (truncated for long texts), then Share (JSON as a file) or Copy. A roster with errors can still be exported; a banner says so. .ros/.rosz and more layouts come later. Stored mode (built in battle-augur plan 2G part 1; Export on a roster without its data, Export as it was on a changed one): title Export roster with "{name} · read only" below, three radio rows: Battle Augur roster file ("The roster as stored. It opens fully once the data is back.", always), Text and New Recruit JSON ("As last saved {relative date}" from the saved snapshot, else disabled with "Needs the game data"), then the preview, Copy and Share.
reactNative.accessibility: Label the format control, keep the preview selectable, and announce the copied toast.

reactNative.behavior: Confirm destructive removal and retain list position.
reactNative.accessibility: Give add and remove actions distinct labels.

reactNative.behavior: Handle cached account data and sign-in transitions.
reactNative.accessibility: Do not expose email as the sole account identifier.

reactNative.behavior: Use the native navigation library and safe-area insets.
reactNative.accessibility: Expose tab role, selected state, and badge value.

reactNative.behavior: Keep the roster list available when organization controls are dismissed; adapt the organizer between an inline panel and a sheet.
reactNative.accessibility: Name search, folder, game-system, and tag controls and preserve the active filter when the panel closes.

reactNative.behavior: Allow the introductory prompt to be dismissed without hiding the empty roster state or creation action.
reactNative.accessibility: Give the close button a descriptive label and retain logical focus after dismissal.

reactNative.behavior: Built in plan 1A (DEC-021/022): every tab shows; a tab or feature that is not built shows this card (icon, Coming soon, title, what it will do, its tier and catalogue IDs, a note that it is switched on for testing). Tab roots keep the tab header with the avatar.
reactNative.accessibility: The title is a header; chips carry words.

reactNative.behavior: Built in plan 1A (DEC-022): hidden until seven quick taps on App → About → Version (each within 1.5 s; a toast confirms; saved in preferences); always shown in dev builds. Developer holds the performance overlay, Imports at once (1 / 2, segmented; for measuring concurrent installs) with install measurements (last 10 lines, Copy / Clear; plan 2E part 3), feature flags by area with tier and build status, the component gallery and engine bench, the engine worker, and Hide developer options.
reactNative.accessibility: The version row stays a plain row; the unlock toast is announced.

reactNative.behavior: Use consistent recovery actions and preserve content during refresh.
reactNative.accessibility: Announce state transitions and make recovery actions reachable.

reactNative.behavior: Implemented 5A. Roster unit and configuration rows push options above the mounted roster session. Render worker unit models: nested named groups, selected/max counts, per-choice cost deltas, optional toggles, quantities and included rows. Optional radio groups always list a None radio row first (checked while nothing is chosen), so choosing never inserts a row above the options (UX-004); required groups retain a choice; a chosen radio does not look disabled. Model cards expand inline loadout groups, with per-model cost and stack count. Hard limits stop; soft minimum/maximum violations keep editing and show text plus an error glyph. Model bounds account for sibling stacks. Existing instances retain their loadouts on quantity edits. Selected options with drill targets open nested options and breadcrumbs. While a command runs or facts refresh, a small spinner in room kept next to the cost chip is the only change: controls are not dimmed (taps are ignored), and the unit's issues stay shown while their check is pending, so nothing moves or flashes (UX-004). A model or quantity pinned at its evaluated min = max shows its count and limits but no stepper (UX-003). Missing selections and failures have recovery actions. Show hidden is explicit; selected hidden options remain visible. The wider original unit-detail design retains later split, association, profile, reference and action specifications.
reactNative.accessibility: Use named radio groups, checked/disabled states on choices and switches, labelled adjustable steppers, busy status, descriptive drill buttons, and text plus icons for invalid counts. Wrap long names and cost lines.

reactNative.behavior: Implemented 5B (UD-2, UD-6). Options | Profile tabs below the header chips, per screen instance and kept while drilling. Profile renders the worker's tables: one card per profile type, a horizontal ScrollView when wider than the card, columns sized to their text and the OS font scale; columns whose values wrap are left-aligned and share the room left in the card. Rules with a description expand on tap; categories follow. On Options a category chip opens the Profile tab with that category marked. Formatting codes in data text are rendered (see Formatted Data Text).
reactNative.accessibility: Tablist/tab roles with selected state; each table row is one element read as 'name, column: value, ...' (missing values read 'none'); header row hidden from screen readers; rules are buttons with expanded state; chips are buttons with a hint.

reactNative.behavior: Implemented. One section per association of the shown selection (worker UnitDetailModel.links), named after the association, with 'linked/max linked' or 'n linked', 'Needs n more link(s)' for an unmet minimum and 'Over maximum'. Max 1: radio rows; another target sends one setAssociation (moves the link), the linked one sends clearAssociation. Otherwise check rows that stay editable at the maximum. Candidates come from the worker (ineligible units hidden, full ones offered); a linked unit no longer eligible stays, marked, so it can be unlinked. Edits go through the shared edit session (Undo/Redo, Saved). Roster rows show the first link as a one-line caption with '+N'; links inside the same unit are left out.
reactNative.accessibility: Radio group or checkboxes with checked/disabled state and Link/Unlink hints; 44 pt rows; the row's accessibility label names every link.

reactNative.behavior: Implemented. A top-level unit whose own association has action group is drawn under its target unit (same force, not hidden, not itself nested) inside the target's slot card, right after it, indented with a corner connector. Its own slot still counts it (used, points, state, markers) and shows a muted 'N shown under linked units' line. The nesting link is left out of both rows' link captions. Diagnostics jumps open the slot that holds the nested row.
reactNative.accessibility: Nested rows keep tap, swipe and custom actions; the label adds 'Attached to {unit} ({association})'; the slot header label includes the elsewhere count.

reactNative.behavior: Implemented. Renders data text formatting codes in rule descriptions and profile table cells: **bold**, *italic*, ^^keyword^^ in the accent text tone (semibold, bold inside bold), line breaks, blank-line paragraph gaps, '- ' and '■ ' lines as bullets with a hanging indent. Unmatched markers stay literal. Column widths use the plain text. Exports keep the codes.
reactNative.accessibility: Screen readers read the text without markers; bullet glyphs are hidden; follows OS font scaling.

reactNative.behavior: Implemented (UX-005). Every option section, at every nesting level and inside model loadouts, has a header button that folds its own body; sections start expanded. The header keeps the name, 'x/y selections', limits and errors, and a folded header with an error beneath it adds 'Issues inside'. Folding a parent hides its descendants but keeps their folds. The screen holds the folds, keyed by the worker's section key (parent selection and group path), so they survive worker refreshes, the Profile tab and a collapsed model card, and are never shared between selections or groups. Folding is presentation only: it works while read-only or busy, and controls and commands are unchanged.
reactNative.accessibility: The header is a button with expanded state, a label of name, counter and issue note, and a Hides/Shows hint; 44 pt minimum height.

groups.label: Design Gallery UI
groups.description: Web-only review and gallery tooling; excluded from the React Native product implementation.
